intro: The night sky has inspired human creativity for millennia, and celestial symbols remain among the most popular Unicode decorations. From full moon phase sequences to crescent moons, suns, and cosmic sparkles, these characters create a dreamy, stargazing aesthetic. Use them in bios, captions, and usernames on any platform that supports Unicode text.

paragraphs: This readout works out the Moon's phase for your own date, in your browser: it counts the time since a known new moon and divides it by the average lunar cycle of 29.53 days. The real Moon runs up to about 18 hours ahead of or behind that average, so the phase shown is within a day of the exact one.

Moon emoji are drawn the way the Moon looks from the Northern Hemisphere. South of the equator the lit side is reversed, so a waxing crescent looks like 🌘 there. Choose Southern and the readout switches to the emoji that matches your sky. It starts on Southern when your device's time zone is south of the equator.
Copy a complete celestial sequence in one click: the eight moon phases in astronomical order, plus the Sun Progression cycle from sunrise to night.

Unicode’s moon signs come from two separate worlds. ☽ and ☾ belong to the astronomical symbol set, where they sit beside the planet signs: technical notation, single-colour, in use for centuries in almanacs and ephemerides. The moon-phase emoji 🌑 to 🌘 arrived only with the emoji set and show the moon as a picture. In practice, for an astrology or astronomy text the single-colour signs are right, and for a bio or a message the emoji are. Both mean the same thing, but they speak in different registers.
